title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 138
paragraphs: These Pelasgians, now dwelling on Lemnos, wanted to get revenge on the Athenians. Having full knowledge of the Athenian festivals, they fitted out fifty-oared galleys and lay in wait for the Athenian women while they were celebrating a festival of Artemis at Brauron. They seized a number of them, sailed off, and carried them to Lemnos, where they kept them as concubines. When these women gradually bore more and more children, they took pains to teach their sons both the Attic language and Athenian manners. The boys would not mix with the sons of the Pelasgian wives, and if any one of them was struck by one of those other boys, they all came in a body to his defense; moreover, they claimed authority over the other boys and had the better of them with ease. The Pelasgians, observing this, took counsel, and a fear came over them: if these boys were already showing themselves resolved to stand together against the sons of the lawful wives, and were already trying to assert authority over them from the start, what would they do when they grew up to be men? So they decided to kill the sons of the Athenian women, and this they did; and they killed their mothers as well. From this deed, and from what was done before — when the Lemnian women killed their husbands, Thoas and the rest — it has become a custom throughout Greece that any act of exceptional cruelty is called a “Lemnian deed.”
